# FinOps report: inventory-service

Pricing: `static-2026-10` (us-west-2, USD, 730 h/month) · analysis date 2026-10-20

## Summary

The legacy EC2 monolith costs USD 71.89/month. The EKS + RDS target as designed costs USD 622.88/month (8.7x today) but the optimized version costs USD 207.57/month, staying within the USD 450/month budget (headroom USD 242.43). The increase over today is USD 135.68/month (2.9x) and buys HA, managed PostgreSQL with automated backups, and autoscaling for the 3x traffic growth.

> ⚠️ Kubernetes 1.33 is in EKS extended support since 2026-07-29: +$365/month. Upgrade to 1.36 (standard support) in terraform/variables.tf → kubernetes_version.

| Scenario | USD/month | vs current | Within USD 450 budget |
|---|---:|---:|:---:|
| Current: EC2 t3.large monolith | 71.89 | - | yes |
| Target as designed (terraform + k8s) | 622.88 | +550.99 | **no** |
| **Target optimized (recommended)** | **207.57** | +135.68 | yes |

## Why the target costs more, and what it buys

The optimized target costs 2.9x the current monolith but this pays for production-grade availability: no single point of failure (2+ nodes across AZs, Multi-AZ RDS), a managed PostgreSQL database with automated backups and security updates, and Kubernetes autoscaling to handle the planned 3x traffic growth. Fixed costs include the EKS control plane (USD 0.10/h), a single NAT gateway (USD 0.045/h + USD 0.045/GB egress), an Application Load Balancer (USD 0.0225/h + USD 0.008/LCU), and the Multi-AZ RDS instance (USD 0.032/h). The applied optimizations (K8s version upgrade, right-sizing, log hygiene, savings plan and RDS reserved instance) reduce the target from USD 622.88/month to USD 207.57/month.

## What you pay for

| Category | Current | As designed | Optimized | What it buys |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| control-plane | 0.00 | 438.00 | 73.00 | Managed Kubernetes API and etcd across 3 AZs, patched by AWS. Fixed per cluster, not per load. |
| compute | 60.74 | 49.06 | 17.67 | The nodes that run the pods: 2+ nodes in different AZs, so losing a node or an AZ keeps the API up. |
| database | 0.00 | 52.05 | 38.55 | Managed PostgreSQL with a synchronous standby in a second AZ, automated backups and point-in-time recovery (RPO 15 min, RTO 1 h) instead of a SQLite file on one disk. |
| network | 8.15 | 71.47 | 71.47 | Load balancer with health checks across AZs, NAT egress for private nodes, public IPv4 addresses and internet egress. |
| storage | 3.00 | 3.30 | 3.30 | Node root volumes and the private container registry. |
| observability | 0.00 | 8.60 | 3.18 | Central JSON logs (NFR5) instead of log files on one server's disk. |
| security | 0.00 | 0.40 | 0.40 | Database credentials in Secrets Manager instead of in the code (SEC1). |
| **Total** | **71.89** | **622.88** | **207.57** | |

## Recommendations

| ID | Recommendation | Saves USD/month | Effort | Risk | Applies to | Why |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| FO-01 | Create the cluster on a Kubernetes version in EKS standard support | 365.00 | low | low | terraform | ⚠️ Kubernetes 1.33 is in EKS extended support since 2026-07-29: +$365/month. Upgrade to 1.36 (standard support) in terraform/variables.tf → kubernetes_version. |
| FO-02 | Right-size pods and pick the cheapest node type that fits | 24.53 | low | low | k8s | Right-size pods to 200m/128Mi CPU/memory and pick the cheapest node type that fits 6 replicas + system pods: 2 x t4g.small |
| FO-03 | Log retention and noise reduction | 5.42 | low | low | k8s | Reduce log ingestion from 10 GB to 6 GB/month by setting a 30-day retention and dropping probe/EKS api logs |
| FO-04 | 1-year Compute Savings Plan (no upfront) for the node baseline | 6.86 | low | low | process | Commit to the always-on node spend for 1 year (no upfront) to save on the on-demand rate |
| FO-05 | 1-year RDS reserved instance (no upfront) | 13.50 | low | low | process | Reserve the Multi-AZ RDS instance for 1 year (no upfront) to save on the on-demand rate |
| FO-06 | Spot capacity for dev/test node groups (dev/test only) | 16.53 | low | low | process | Dev/test tolerates interruptions and downtime. |
| FO-07 | Scale dev/test nodes to zero outside 08:00-18:00 on weekdays (dev/test only) | 17.14 | low | low | process | Dev/test tolerates interruptions and downtime. |

| FO-09 | Monitor node utilization and plan a node type upgrade | not quantified | medium | low | k8s | t4g.small is the cheapest that fits today; as traffic grows to 3x the pods will need more CPU/memory and likely a larger node |

**Dev/test environments** (not in the production totals):

- Spot capacity for dev/test node groups: saves 16.53 USD/month per environment (`2 x (0.0168 - 0.00548) USD/h x 730 h`)
- Scale dev/test nodes to zero outside 08:00-18:00 on weekdays: saves 17.14 USD/month per environment (`2 x 0.0168 USD/h x (730 - 220) h`)

## Right-sizing

| | Declared (k8s manifests) | Measured (container) | Legacy-VM estimate (upper bound) | Recommended |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pod requests | 100m CPU, 128Mi | - | 544Mi memory | 200m CPU, 128Mi |
| Pod limits | 500m CPU, 256Mi | - | 832Mi memory | 500m CPU, 256Mi |
| Replicas (HPA) | 2-6 | - | - | 2-6 |
| Nodes | 2 x t4g.medium | - | - | 2-4 x t4g.small |
| Database | db.t4g.small | - | - | db.t4g.small |

The legacy-VM estimate (544Mi request / 832Mi limit) starts from the whole VM's memory in use and only subtracts a nominal 1024 MiB for the OS, nginx and agents, so page cache and everything else on the host still count. The container data (declared 128Mi) is what the pod really needs, so the recommendation keeps 128Mi / 256Mi and uses the VM figure only as an upper bound.

How the pod size was derived (CPU from the legacy VM's p95, memory from the container):

- `vm_cpu_p95 = 2 vCPU x 1000 x 12% = 240m (whole VM at 40 rps peak)`
- `cpu_request = ceil50(240m / 2 replicas / 70% HPA) = 200m`
- `cpu_limit = ceil50(200m x 2.5) = 500m`
- `memory_request = 128Mi, memory_limit = 256Mi (k8s manifests)`
- `memory upper bound (legacy VM): 8 GiB x 18% - 1024Mi OS/agents = 451Mi; ceil32(x 1.2) = 544Mi request, ceil32(x 1.5) = 832Mi limit`
- `replicas: peak 2, with 3x growth 6 (each pod absorbs 140m before scaling)`

Growth check: at 3x traffic the HPA needs 6 replicas on 2 nodes: 207.57 USD/month.

## Assumptions

- Month = 730 h. us-west-2 prices from `static-2026-10` (fetched 2026-10-19); Linux on-demand unless stated.
- Legacy utilization (estimate): CPU p95 12%, memory 18% of 2 vCPU / 8 GiB.
- Nominal usage (no input provides it): 50 GB/month internet egress (same before and after), 20 GB through NAT, 1 ALB LCU, 10 GB/month CloudWatch Logs, 1 GB ECR.
- An internet-facing ALB is assumed for the API even when the manifests have no Ingress yet; it uses one public IPv4 address per AZ. The legacy VM has one public IPv4 address.
- Node fit: EKS AL2023 kubelet reservations, 4 DaemonSets (VPC CNI, kube-proxy, pod identity, fluent-bit) and system pods (CoreDNS x2, metrics-server, AWS Load Balancer Controller x2); at least 2 nodes and N+1 at baseline.
- Nodes are sized for HPA max replicas all month: the design has no node autoscaler (Karpenter or Cluster Autoscaler would let the baseline shrink).
- Memory right-sizing uses container data first (manifest); the legacy-VM figure (memory in use minus a 1024 MiB OS/agents baseline) is only an upper bound. Confirm with `kubectl top pods` or VPA recommendations after the first week.
- Savings Plan and RI rates are 1-year, no upfront (Compute Savings Plan rate from the Savings Plans API).
- Kubernetes 1.33: EXTENDED_SUPPORT on 2026-10-20 (standard support ended 2026-07-29; extended support adds 0.5 USD/h).
- Not modelled: RDS backups within the free allocation, the S3 reports bucket (cents), t4g CPU credit surplus (utilization is low), the 100 GB/month free egress tier.

## Risks and follow-ups

- The EKS cluster runs in extended support (K8s 1.33) and must be upgraded to a standard-support version such as 1.36.
- The single NAT gateway is a shared egress point; if one AZ fails the whole cluster loses internet access. Consider a second NAT gateway in a different AZ if egress is mission-critical.
- The node type t4g.small is the cheapest that fits the right-sized pods; monitor utilization as traffic grows and be ready to scale nodes.
